en: The *Aṅgacakranirdeśasūtra* Spoken by the Deva Nandikeśvara,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
At that time, the deity Nandikeśvara surveyed all men and women in the world,
[observing] the good and evil karma they had experienced due to the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*) present at the time of their birth.
Until the end of their lifespan, throughout that interval,
they may be noble or lowly, wealthy or poor;
they may possess filial piety or loyalty, and they may be fond of literature or fond of martial arts.
As for those who are handsome or ugly, dull-witted or intelligent,
afflicted by illness or met with untimely death, widowed, orphaned, or destitute,
as well as those who are fierce and stubborn or gentle and submissive.
Their speech was correct and their conduct upright; they possessed self-awareness and a sense of shame.
They were erudite in the heavenly scriptures and discerning in worldly affairs.
Some held the Buddha-dharma in high esteem and delighted in cultivating virtuous deeds.
Some may admire demons and spirits, believing in heterodoxy and committing evil;
others may delight in roaming mountains and waters, following their natural inclinations to perfect their true nature;
and still others may enjoy engaging in commerce and trade, dealing in precious goods.
Whether one is fond of giving or is miserly and greedy,
these states are both manifested through prominent physical marks on the limbs,
appearing as banners, conchs, patterns, or moles.
All beauty and ugliness are received together within a single body;
this is likewise due to causes and conditions from past lives meeting with the current planetary influences.
Fearing that you may not yet understand, I shall briefly proclaim this for you.
Furthermore, when the Sun is in the mansion of Aja (the Ram),
it is directly in the asterisms of Ārdrā, the full portion of Rohiṇī, and one part of Mṛgaśirā.
For those born on that day:
His appearance was dignified and his limbs were slender and exquisite;
he was filial toward his parents and respectful in serving his elders;
he possessed many kinsmen and an abundance of servants and attendants.
He is courageous and spirited, possesses great merit,
cannot endure hunger and cold,
delights in the Dharma, and knows shame and remorse.
With a firm resolve for generosity,
his words and deeds were truthful and his insight was clear;
he thus deserved the King’s affection and respect, and was venerated by the multitude.
The eyes are dull and greedy for forms;
one delights much in wandering about, and throughout one's life there is an abundance [of such activity].
There is dental disease as well as jaundice.
Regarding his lifespan, he may meet an untimely death in the fourth year after birth due to a fire-related disaster;
at the age of eighteen, he is likewise liable to die prematurely;
and at the age of twenty-five, he shall encounter the danger of tigers and wolves.
It also presides over death in the midst of the ocean and the calamity of untimely demise.

If one encounters the auspicious luminaries shining upon them, their lifespan will be extended to one hundred years; however, within the eighth month, they will encounter the planet Mars (Agni) and the lunar mansion Mṛgaśiras.
He passed away at midnight on that very day.
Furthermore, when the Sun was in Taurus,
it was in conjunction with the lunar mansion Mṛgaśirā for three degrees, and with both Pūrvabhadrapadā and Uttarabhadrapadā for two degrees each.
Those born on this day, whether male or female,
will possess dignified and handsome features with slender limbs.
Their faces will bear birthmarks or moles, which presage great wealth and constant enjoyment of happiness.
He will have many kinsmen and numerous servants,
yet his temperament will be stern and unbending, making him ill-suited for a wife or concubines;
he will experience hardship from a young age.
In his later years, he further obtained the wealth and property of his parents and enjoyed happiness.
He possessed a refined spirit, was skilled in craftsmanship, and had clear insight;
his undertakings were steadfast, and he delighted in practicing generosity.
Craving the taste of food brings many afflictions and throat ailments;
at twenty-five years of age, his life is destined to end prematurely.
However, if at this time he is further graced by the auspicious influence of favorable planetary conjunctions, [he may escape].
Transforming evil into good, one attains an extended lifespan reaching a hundred years. Subsequently,
one suffers from the affliction of wind-madness during the ninth month,
under the influence of the planet Mercury (Budha) and the lunar mansion Piṣya (Revatī).
The day-duty (zhírì) concludes at the site of the holy traces.
Furthermore, in the Yin-yang Palace, it corresponds to the planet Mercury;
the day-duty resides in two degrees of the lunar mansion *Zēn* (Aśvinī), and three degrees each in *Zuǐ* (Bharaṇī) and *Jǐng* (Kṛttikā).
Those born on this day, whether male or female,
are by nature gentle and virtuous, possess upright physical features,
speak with truthfulness, and are eloquent and quick-witted in conversation.
In friendships and social obligations, his commitment is long-lasting;
he has a preference for fragrant flowers and a craving for fine flavors;
by nature he is humorous and jovial, and he is deeply attached to women.
Beholding beauty with one's own eyes, the soul is as if lost;
that which is seen in various illusory arts is cherished,
while that which is attained through the practice of the methods of accomplishment is certain.
If he studies the methods for subduing dragons and consecrating water,
he will attain the most refined mastery of these two arts.
After enduring hardships from his youth until middle age, he will finally achieve renown, and all who see him will hold him in high esteem.
From birth until the fifth year, there is the danger of premature death.
During this period of potential death,
if one encounters the auspicious planets shining upon them, the evil may be transformed into good.
He shall attain an extended lifespan reaching eighty years.
Within the tenth month, encountering the planet Mercury (Budha) and the lunar mansion Ārdrā,
he will pass away from illness at midday on his appointed day.
Furthermore, when the Moon is in the house of Cancer (Karkaṭa-rāśi) and is directly aligned with the lunar mansions of Aśleṣā, Mūla, and the full extent of Pūrvaphalgunī,
for those— whether male or female— who are born on such a day:
His physical frame was tall and slender, and his innate nature was gentle and virtuous.
Possessing wisdom and the capacity for endurance,
he was filial toward his parents and received their greatest affection and favor.
On his hands and the soles of his feet, he possesses the marks of the lotus, the conch, the wheel, and the auspicious fruit;
he has many wives, concubines, and retinues, as well as numerous servants.
In his youth he was humble and lowly, but in his later years he became wealthy.
Joyful in the Dharma and courageous, he delighted in practicing generosity,
making offerings to the noble ones, sages, and his teachers.
By nature he loved traveling afar.
After his birth, when he reached the age of twenty, he was destined to fall from a tree;
because of this, he met with a premature death.
At this time, if one encounters the auspicious planets shining upon them,
evil shall be transformed into good and their lifespan extended to eighty years.
This occurs in the eleventh month under the constellation Ārdrā and the planet Venus.
He passed away at midnight on that very day.
Furthermore, when the Sun was in Leo,
it was positioned within one degree each of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) of Jyeṣṭhā and Viśākhā.
Those born on this day will be impetuous by nature and prone to anger in their conduct;
they will give birth to two or three children whom they will love more than their own lives.
Though possessing abundant wealth and treasures, his mind was always content;
he delighted in making offerings to all worthies and sages,
and as a person, he was neither dissolute nor extravagant, being naturally self-sufficient.
They prefer eating meat and also enjoy eating fish.
Whether traveling to other lands, they do not suffer from hunger or cold;
they are constantly afraid of illness but have no fear of great floods.
If one reaches the age of fifteen and encounters the difficulty of an untimely death, yet is graced by the aspect of auspicious planets,
this evil may be transformed into good, and one’s lifespan may be extended to a hundred years.
This applies within the twelve months when the planet Saturn and its corresponding lunar mansions are encountered.
The day-duty (nakṣatra) falls on the northern bank of the Ganges at the time of death.
Furthermore, the constellation of the Twin Maidens (Aśleṣā) is governed by Mercury;
the day-duty resides in three degrees of the constellation Swātī (Śraviṣṭhā), and two degrees each in the constellations of the Tortoise (Jyeṣṭhā) and the Horns (Viśākhā).
Those born on this day, whether male or female,
will have monkey-like faces and wide eyes, with moles beneath their ribs;
people will look upon them with respect and affection.
They delight in the Dharma and cherish fragrant flowers;
though they may be young and of humble station, they will possess abundant wealth in their later years.
However, they will frequently suffer from illness, particularly afflictions of the eyes.
Fortunately, in other lands it is not customary to have concubines;
yet whenever he beholds one of beauty, his spirit and soul lose their composure.
At the age of thirty-some years, he faces the peril of an untimely death.
When facing the calamity of untimely death, he was graced by the auspicious influence of favorable planets;
thus, evil was transformed into good, and his life was extended to eighty years.
Within the first lunar month, he passed away due to an illness involving sores.
Furthermore, when Libra is presided over by Venus (Śukra),
with the asterism Jyeṣṭhā occupying two degrees and both Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī each occupying three degrees;
on such a day, those of either gender who are born—
He was filial and obedient toward his parents, and his fortune and status were naturally secure.
By nature, however, he was impetuous and prone to anger;
yet his insight was clear and penetrating, and he was capable of discerning the most subtle details.
Furthermore, he possesses a dignified bearing and is capable of great fortitude and patience.
He excels in befriending others, is humorous and witty, and has a fondness for beauty.
He frequently travels abroad.
Alternatively, one may experience pleasant matters out of their proper sequence.
The palms of the hands possess the marks of banners and canopies;
until the age of twenty-two, there will be the danger of an untimely death.
If, during a time of untimely death or calamity, one encounters the auspicious influence of a benefic planet,
evil may be transformed into good and one's life-span extended to ninety-seven years.
However, within the second month, if death occurs on a day governed by the planet Mars (Bhauma) and the lunar mansion Rohiṇī (Mṛgaśiras), [the life-span will not be so prolonged].
Furthermore, when Mars is in the sign of Scorpio,
it is directly aligned with one part each of the lunar mansions Jyeṣṭhā, Viśākhā, and Anurādhā. On such a day,
if a male or female is born, [the following shall be known].
The primary lord is harmonious with those of sharp faculties, for whom what is studied is easily accomplished.
Regarding the meaning of the person's character: although their wealth and treasures may be abundant, they will either accumulate or disperse them.
Upon reaching the age of eighteen, there will be perils from snakes, scorpions, tigers, and wolves.
Upon reaching the age of twenty, he again encountered the calamity of an untimely death.
Had he been graced by the auspicious influence of favorable planets at the time of that fatal crisis,
the evil would have been transformed into good, and his life span extended to seventy-seven years.
Within three months, death shall occur on a Tuesday coinciding with the lunar mansion Śravaṇā.
Furthermore, in the sign of Sagittarius (Dhanus), Jupiter is the presiding planet;
it governs one part each of the lunar mansions Mūla, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, and Uttarāṣāḍhā.
For those born on this day, whether male or female,
they will possess a physical form that is upright and dignified, and be endowed with auspicious marks.
By nature they will be gentle and virtuous, and their observance of the precepts will be firm and steadfast.
In all that they say, they strive for truth;
they possess sufficient wisdom and delight in discussing the meaning of the Dharma throughout their entire lives.
He will always dwell in great wealth;
in his youth, he will also discover hidden treasure,
but at the age of eighteen, he will encounter the calamity of an untimely death.
If, during a time of untimely death or calamity, one is graced by the auspicious influence of a favorable planet,
evil may be transformed into good and one's lifespan extended to seventy-seven years.
Within the fourth month, one encounters the planet Venus (Suvarṇa) and the lunar mansion Rohiṇī.
The officer on duty fasted and ended his life by throwing himself into the water.
Furthermore, in the palace of Makara, it corresponds to the day of the planet Saturn;
the officer on duty is in the third degree of the lunar mansion Dou (Uttarāṣāḍhā), and two degrees each in the mansions Niu (Rohiṇī) and Nü (Śravaṇā).
Those born on this day, whether male or female, will have upright physical features but dark moles in their private parts.
By nature they are irascible and frequently prone to anger; their eyes are furtive and their countenance is dull.
However, he possessed a spirit and wisdom that were extraordinary;
he was fully devoted to loyalty and filial piety, had many friends,
and his mind was courageous and fond of battle.
He is fond of song and dance and skilled in the arts;
he is also fond of perfumes and flowers and has many wives and concubines.
When he reaches the age of thirty, he faces the calamity of premature death.
When facing the calamity of untimely death, if one encounters the auspicious planets' illumination,
evil shall be transformed into good and one’s lifespan extended to seventy-five years.
Within the fifth month, one will encounter the planet Saturn and the lunar mansion Wei (Apabharaṇī).
The day-duty officer (zhírì) passes away.
Furthermore, when the planet Saturn is in the house of Aquarius (Rāśi),
the day-duty falls on the two divisions of the lunar mansion Virgo (Jyeṣṭhā), and three divisions each of the lunar mansions Pūrvāṣāḍhā and Uttarāṣāḍhā.
Those born on this day, whether male or female,
will become great lords of wealth and constantly enjoy happiness;
they will have many kinsmen and numerous servants.
Yet he was intensely devoted to filial care for his parents;
though he had a wife, he did not guard their wealth.
Among the children born to him, some met with premature death.
His eyes were shrewd and perceptive, yet he possessed a sense of integrity and righteousness.
He was discerning in all matters, and his actions were enduring.
By nature, he was not stingy, but delighted solely in practicing generosity.
The wealth and possessions he had accumulated were also dispersed;
he gave rise to fear of tigers and wolves,
and when he reached the age of eighteen, he encountered the peril of tigers and wolves.
During times of adversity, if one encounters the auspicious influence of favorable planets,
evil shall be transformed into good and one's lifespan will be extended to eighty-four years.
Within six months, one will encounter the Sun and the lunar mansion of Aśvinī (Kwei).
The day-duty officer died from an ulcerous sore.
Furthermore, in the sign of Pisces, Jupiter presides;
the day-duty shifts are each one part among the lunar mansions of Śravaṇā, Dhanisthā, and Rohiṇī.
Those born on this day, whether male or female,
will have well-proportioned bodies and shrewd,
intelligent eyes; they will have many wives, concubines, and kinsmen, as well as numerous servants.
By nature he is impetuous and frequently prone to anger.
He possesses great physical strength, craves meat,
and furthermore, has a fondness for eating fish.
However, he delights in practicing generosity and making offerings to the worthy and holy;
he loves fragrant flowers and excels in technical arts;
yet he is greedily attached to beautiful forms and is jealous of women.
One who speaks much truth may also incur the fault of slandering their teacher.
One who suffers from ear ailments will also enjoy a long life.
At the age of eighteen, one faces the danger of falling from a tree or a wall.
If one encounters the auspicious planets shining upon them, evil may be transformed into good;
they shall attain an extended lifespan reaching ninety-five years. Within the seventh month, they will encounter the planet Saturn and the lunar mansion (nakṣatra) Bhittī.
The duty officer died from an ulcerous sore.
Furthermore, it is taught that the various lunar mansions are subsumed within the three realms of existence (*gati*).
Specifically, nine mansions—namely, Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, and Maghā—are subsumed within the celestial realm (*devagati*).
The nine lunar mansions of Wei, Miao, Zui, Liu, Xing, Jiao, Di, Xin, and Wei comprise the realm of rākṣasas;
the nine lunar mansions of Ji, Shi, Zhang, Bi, Nu, Wei, Dou, Bi, and Yi comprise the realm of humans.
If those born under the influence of the various constellations of the celestial realms,
whether male or female, shall all dwell in wealth and nobility;
their descendants will flourish, and they will possess the most supreme of all auspicious fortunes.
At that time, the deity Nandikeśvara,
having taught the *cakravarti* [wheel] for all men and women in the world, withdrew with joy.
The Cakravarti-sūtra Spoken by the Deva Nandikeśvara.
